content: 1. Eslcarbazepine Acetate: This drug reduces the levels or effects of lopinavir and ritonavir by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for reduced efficacy. 2. Ritonavir and Esomeprazole: Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of esomeprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 3. Lopinavir and Estradiol: Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, ritonavir increases estradiol levels through both CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for potential toxicity. 4. Estradiol Vaginal: Both lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels or effects of estradiol vaginal formulations via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 5. Estrogens (Conjugated Synthetic): Lopinavir and ritonavir increase the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir also influences P-glycoprotein transport. Monitor for increased estrogenic effects or toxicity. 6. Eszopiclone: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase eszopiclone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification is recommended, with a reduced starting dose of 1 mg/day for eszopiclone. 7. Ethosuximide: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase ethosuximide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for potential toxicity. 8. Etonogestrel: Ritonavir increases etonogestrel levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Etoposide: Both lopinavir and ritonavir increase etoposide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir also influences P-glycoprotein transport. Monitor for toxicity. 10. Etrasimod: Co-administration with lopinavir may increase the risk of QT prolongation and Torsades de Pointes. Monitor heart rate and QT interval closely. 11. Etravirine: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase etravirine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while etravirine decreases lopinavir levels. Monitor for altered drug efficacy. 12. Exenatide: Ritonavir and lopinavir reduce the effects of exenatide injectable solutions, potentially due to insulin resistance. Monitor for hyperglycemia. 13. Ezogabine: Co-administration with ritonavir or lopinavir may increase QT prolongation. Monitor QT interval and adjust therapy as needed. 14. Fedratinib: This drug increases ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Adjust doses of CYP2D6 substrates as necessary. 15. Felodipine: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase felodipine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for enhanced effects or toxicity. 16. Fesoterodine: Ritonavir increases fesoterodine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Fluconazole: This drug increases lopinavir and ritonavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for enhanced effects or toxicity. 18. Fludrocortisone: Ritonavir increases fludrocortisone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein transport. Monitor for enhanced corticosteroid effects. 19. Flunisolide (Inhaled): Lopinavir and ritonavir increase flunisolide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for systemic corticosteroid effects. 20. Flurazepam: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase flurazepam levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider alternative benzodiazepines or reduce the dose. 21. Fluticasone Furoate: Monitor closely. 22. Fluvastatin: Ritonavir increases fluvastatin toxicity, potentially due to OATP1B1 inhibition. Monitor for myopathy. 23. Fluvoxamine: This drug increases lopinavir and ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for enhanced effects. 24. Fosamprenavir: Co-administration with ritonavir or lopinavir increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitor closely. 25. Fosaprepitant: This drug increases ritonavir and lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for enhanced effects. 26. Fosphenytoin: This drug decreases ritonavir and lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein transport. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 27. Fostamatinib: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase fostamatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein transport. Monitor for toxicities and adjust doses as needed. 28. Fostemsavir: Co-administration with lopinavir may increase QT prolongation. Monitor QT interval closely. 29. Garlic: Garlic reduces ritonavir levels through an unknown mechanism. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 30. Gefitinib: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase gefitinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor for adverse effects. 31. Gentamicin: Ritonavir increases gentamicin levels via P-glycoprotein transport. Monitor for toxicity. 32. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: This combination increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein transport. Monitor for enhanced effects. 33. Glimepiride, Glipizide, and Glyburide: Ritonavir and lopinavir may increase or decrease the levels of these drugs, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Monitor blood glucose levels closely. 34. Grapefruit: Grapefruit increases ritonavir and lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for enhanced effects. 35. Griseofulvin: This drug decreases ritonavir and lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for reduced efficacy. 36. Guanfacine: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase guanfacine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce guanfacine dosage by half and monitor closely. 37. Haloperidol: Ritonavir increases haloperidol levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism, potentially prolonging the QT interval. Monitor for toxicity. 38. Hydrocodone: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase hydrocodone levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Monitor closely. 39. Hydrocortisone: Ritonavir increases hydrocortisone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein transport. Monitor for enhanced corticosteroid effects. 40. Hydromorphone: Ritonavir increases hydromorphone levels via CYP2D6 metabolism. Monitor for toxicity. 41. Idelalisib: This drug increases lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 42. Ifosfamide: Ritonavir and lopinavir decrease ifosfamide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism but may increase effects via CYP2B6 metabolism. Monitor for altered efficacy and toxicity. 43. Iloperidone: Ritonavir increases iloperidone levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Monitor for increased plasma levels and toxicity. 44. Imatinib: Ritonavir increases imatinib levels via P-glycoprotein transport. Monitor for toxicity. 45. Indacaterol (Inhaled): Co-administration with ritonavir or lopinavir may increase QT prolongation. Monitor QT interval closely. 46. Indinavir: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase indinavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitor closely. 47. Insulin (Various Types): Ritonavir and lopinavir reduce the effects of insulin (e.g., aspart, detemir, glargine) due to insulin resistance. Monitor blood glucose levels and adjust therapy as needed. 48. Isoniazid: This drug increases ritonavir and lopinavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for enhanced effects. 49. Istradefylline: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase istradefylline levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit istradefylline dose to 20 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 50. Itraconazole: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase itraconazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit itraconazole dose to 200 mg/day and monitor closely. 51. Ivacaftor: Ritonavir and lopinavir increase ivacaftor levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce ivacaftor dose and monitor for adverse effects. 52. Ivermectin: Ritonavir increases ivermectin levels via P-glycoprotein transport. Monitor for toxicity.
